title: Divis Laboratories Ltd - 532488 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Divi's Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT rose to ₹963 crores (vs ₹864 crores YoY) and PAT to ₹751 crores, while management guided only to "stable" margins.
summary.overview: Divi's reported Q4 FY26 consolidated total income of ₹2,986 crores, PBT of ₹963 crores and PAT of ₹751 crores, including a ₹90 crore forex gain. For FY26, total income rose to ₹11,067 crores from ₹9,712 crores, PAT to ₹2,568 crores from ₹2,191 crores, after a one-time ₹74 crore Labour Code charge. Management said volumes in generics were stable with some pricing pressure, while West Asia-related disruption raised raw material, solvent and freight costs and forced some suppliers to declare force majeure. Management declined to quantify FY27 margins, guiding only to stable margins and double-digit revenue growth.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹2,916 crores in FY25; after ₹74 crore Labour Code exceptional charge

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Volumes stable and healthy through Q4 and FY26 per management, but slight pricing pressure; generic API contracts have variability clauses with reviews as often as every 3 months. FY26 product mix was 45% generics.

segments.name: Custom Synthesis (CS)
segments.commentary: FY26 product mix was 55% CS. Management cited a strong project pipeline across Phase II/III, validation and qualification stages; late life-cycle management volumes may decline as products mature.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Several fragments validated in the quarter with more in pipeline; capabilities include protected amino acids, solid-phase and liquid-phase synthesis, and 3,000-litre SPPS capacity.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Iodine-based contrast media in commercial sales to innovators, supplied in multiple tonnes; Gadolinium compounds still at qualification as customers' products are in Phase II/III.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹946 crores in FY26, up from ₹781 crores in FY25.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth, consistent with its historical stated aim.
Margins expected to 'remain stable' per management; no numerical margin figure given due to current scenario.
Freight-related cost pressures expected to continue in the near term and have been factored into planning.
FY27 capex expected to be roughly constant unless a major CS or new project emerges (CWIP about ₹2,000 crore odd).
Inventory build expected mainly from Q1 FY27 to secure material; no percentage given.
Management expects Kakinada dedicated CS projects to commercialise by 2027, earlier or later, subject to customer regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: ₹2,113 crores CWIP at 31 March 2026; ₹1,544 crores capitalised in FY26, of which about ₹800 crores in Q4.
Kakinada ₹1,500 crore expansion plan; ₹600 crores already capitalised.
Unit 3 (Kakinada) now supports backward integration; select activities moved from Unit 1 and Unit 2 to free GMP space, with moves timed 2-4 months ahead of customer qualification approvals.
Three dedicated CS projects are in validation and supply stage; commercial volumes depend on customer regulatory approval and volume indication.
Capital allocation to CS and peptides, with long-term supply agreements; management guides toward a 2-year range from capex to revenue, but acknowledged timelines from 6 months to 3 years.
demand_pricing: Generic volumes rose in FY26 from existing portfolio; new molecules from customer launches expected to add volume in coming years as products come off patent.
Generic pricing under competitive pressure; customers understanding of market conditions has supported ongoing price discussions.

Raw material prices rising with West Asia conflict; some suppliers invoked force majeure; Ammonia and methanol sourcing affected. Management says cost increases are being passed through where feasible.
No loss of volumes or supply issues with customers reported in Q4; no revenue loss from logistics issues.
Exports about 89% of sales; Europe and US together about 74% of export revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind on raw material availability, and how is methanol sourcing being managed for H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the conflict affected only about one month of FY26 and there were no production stoppages, but sourcing is difficult across solvents and other materials; availability is being reviewed quarterly, with securing supply for the next 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a margin figure, saying it is difficult to project but expected to remain stable; capex for FY27 expected to be constant unless a major CS project emerges.

qa_highlights.question: Why was constant currency growth only about 6% despite capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Most capex was capitalised late in the year; management said it will now track reported revenue growth instead, citing currency volatility, and attributed slower growth to generic pricing pressure rather than a single product.

qa_highlights.question: What would it take to return to 38% margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said generic pricing pressure and higher material costs (rising again due to the war) are the key drags; a return to 38% depends on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: How long from capex to revenue for the new long-term CS supply agreements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for about 2 years but timelines range from 6 months to 3 years, depending on customer approvals and regulatory queries.

qa_highlights.question: How do the rupee depreciation and raw material and freight cost pressures net out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency gains help as the company is export-led, but a rupee reversal would also hurt; about 40% of raw material spend is imported, on total raw material spend of ₹4,000-5,000 crores against ₹11,000 crore revenue.

risks_watch: Raw material and solvent availability and cost, including methanol and ammonia, given force majeure declarations and Middle East-linked disruption.
Freight cost increases expected to continue near term.
Generic pricing pressure, with contract reviews possibly every 3 months.
Timing of CS and dedicated project commercialisation depends on customer regulatory approvals; Kakinada dedicated project targeted around 2027 with no firm date.
Gadolinium contrast media remains at Phase II/III qualification stage, so no near-term revenue visible.
Inventory build expected from Q1 FY27, which could weigh on working capital.
Margin visibility limited; management withheld numerical guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operational continuity and supply reliability, but cautious and guarded on margins and project timelines, repeatedly declining to quantify FY27 margins, capex timing or customer volumes.
key_quotes: Despite these external challenges, the availability of critical raw materials and solvents remained broadly manageable.
So we wouldn't see so much of an effect of what is happening on the yearly results, neither on the quarterly results because it's only one-third.
We are hopeful by 2027 it will be commercialized or earlier or maybe later.
I would say that our supply chain model is pretty stable.
